title: NE LB525: Adopt the Agricultural Data Privacy Act and the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act

obligations: Written consent for the sale of agricultural data shall be obtained through a clear and conspicuous disclosure that is separate from the primary terms of service or data use agreement (Sec. 5(2)).

Beginning on January 1, 2027, every new contract or agreement involving the collection or processing of agricultural data in this state shall contain a specific provision stating that the controller or processor is prohibited from engaging in the sale of such agricultural data without the express written consent of the agricultural producer (Sec. 6(1)).

Any controller or processor in custody or possession of agricultural data shall establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of such agricultural data (Sec. 7(1)).
Such security practices shall be appropriate for the volume and nature of the agricultural data and protect against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or loss (Sec. 7(2)).

An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to each minor account holder that such minor account holder is interacting with artificial intelligence as a persistent visible disclaimer or both at the beginning of each session and appearing at least every three hours in a continuous conversational artificial intelligence service interaction (Sec. 14(1)).

An operator shall, for minor account holders, institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational artificial intelligence service from producing visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct, generating direct statements that the account holder should engage in sexually explicit conduct, or generating statements that sexually objectify the account holder (Sec. 14(3)).

For minor account holders, the operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational artificial intelligence service from generating statements that would lead a reasonable person to believe that they are interacting with a human, including explicit claims that the service is sentient or human, statements that simulate emotional dependence, statements that simulate romantic or sexual innuendos, or role playing of romantic relationships between an adult and a minor (Sec. 14(4)).

An operator shall offer tools for minor account holders, and, when such account holders are younger than thirteen years of age, their parents or guardians, to manage the account holders' privacy and account settings; an operator shall also offer related tools to the parents or guardians of minor account holders thirteen years of age and older, as appropriate based on relevant risks (Sec. 14(5)).

If a reasonable person interacting with a conversational artificial intelligence service would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, an operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose that the conversational artificial intelligence service is artificial intelligence (Sec. 15).

An operator shall adopt a protocol for the conversational artificial intelligence service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self harm that includes, but is not limited to, making reasonable efforts to provide a response to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services (Sec. 16).
prohibitions: A controller or processor shall not engage in the sale of agricultural data without the express written consent of the agricultural producer (Sec. 5(1)).
The nonexclusive right of control granted to a controller or processor under section 4 does not include the power to engage in the sale of such agricultural data (Sec. 4(4)).
Any contract provision that waives or limits the requirements of the Agricultural Data Privacy Act is contrary to public policy and is void and unenforceable (Sec. 6(2)).

An operator shall not provide a minor account holder with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 14(2)).

An operator shall not knowingly and intentionally cause or program a conversational artificial intelligence service to make any representation or statement that explicitly indicates that the conversational artificial intelligence service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (Sec. 17).

notable_exemptions: Agricultural data does not include aggregated data, derived data, or data made available to the general public by an agency as defined in section 84-901 (Sec. 3(3)(b)).

Sale of agricultural data does not include disclosure or transfer to a processor by a controller, use by a processor authorized by a controller, disclosure for providing a service to an agricultural producer, disclosure to an affiliate, disclosure expressly directed in writing by the producer to a designated third party, disclosure required by state or federal law, regulation, subpoena, investigative demand, or court order, disclosure required for compliance with safety, emissions, or environmental obligations, disclosure of information the producer intentionally made available to the general public through mass media without restriction, disclosure as part of a merger, acquisition, bankruptcy, or transaction, or disclosure reasonably necessary to detect, prevent, or respond to fraud, abuse, cybersecurity threat, illegal conduct, data integrity issue, or equipment misuse (Sec. 3(13)(b)).

The Agricultural Data Privacy Act shall not be construed to limit or supersede any duty or obligation imposed by federal law or other Nebraska law, relieve any person from any duty or obligation otherwise imposed by law, impair or affect the terms of any private contract in existence prior to the operative date of section 10, or limit or supersede any duty or obligation imposed by a natural resources district operating pursuant to Chapter 2, article 32, any agency as defined in section 84-901, or any employee or agent of such district or agency when acting in performance of a statutory duty (Sec. 10).

Conversational artificial intelligence service does not include applications primarily designed and marketed for use by developers or researchers, a feature within another software application that is not a conversational artificial intelligence service, applications designed to provide outputs relating to a narrow and discrete topic, applications primarily designed and marketed for commercial use by business entities, speaker and voice command interfaces or voice activated virtual assistants for consumer electronic devices, applications used by a business solely for internal purposes, or applications used by a business solely for customer service or strictly to provide users with information about available commercial services or products, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to the business's customer service (Sec. 13(2)(b)).
Operator does not include mobile application stores or search engines solely because they provide access to a conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 13(6)(b)).

The Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act does not create liability for the developer of an artificial intelligence model for any violation by a conversational artificial intelligence system developed by a third party operator to provide a service for such developer (Sec. 18(4)).
Agricultural data may be withheld from public records unless prior written consent has been obtained from the owner of such agricultural data under the Agricultural Data Privacy Act (Sec. 11(30)).

What it does

The law adopts the Agricultural Data Privacy Act, which gives agricultural producers ownership and control of agricultural data originating from their farm, land, devices, and equipment, and prohibits controllers and processors from selling that data without express written consent while requiring reasonable data security. It also adopts the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act, which imposes disclosure, content prevention, privacy tool, and crisis protocol duties on operators of conversational artificial intelligence services, especially for minor account holders. It amends the public records law to allow withholding agricultural data absent prior written consent from the owner.

Who it applies to

  • Controllers and processors of agricultural data collected, produced, or generated in Nebraska (Sec. 3, Sec. 5, Sec. 7)
  • Agricultural producers who own or control agricultural data (Sec. 4)
  • Operators of conversational artificial intelligence services accessible to the general public (Sec. 13, Sec. 14)
  • Minor account holders and their parents or guardians (Sec. 14)
  • Public entities holding agricultural data records (Sec. 11)

Effective date

Sections 12 through 18, the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act, become operative on July 1, 2027 (Sec. 19). The other sections become operative on their effective date, which is not stated in the text (Sec. 19). The requirement for new contracts involving agricultural data to contain a specific no sale provision begins on January 1, 2027 (Sec. 6).

Key definitions

  • Agricultural data: any agronomic data, climate and weather data, land data, livestock data, management data, and sustainability data that is collected, produced, or generated in this state and is linked or reasonably linked to an identified or reasonably identifiable agricultural producer; does not include aggregated data, derived data, or data made available to the general public by an agency as defined in section 84-901 (Sec. 3(3))
  • Agricultural producer: the person that is the owner, lessee, or renter of the farm, livestock, land, device, or equipment from which agricultural data originates (Sec. 3(4))
  • Controller: a person who or entity that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purpose and means of processing agricultural data (Sec. 3(7))
  • Processor: a person who or entity that processes agricultural data on behalf of a controller (Sec. 3(12))
  • Sale of agricultural data: the exchange of agricultural data for monetary or other valuable consideration by a controller or processor to a third party, with listed exclusions (Sec. 3(13))
  • Aggregated data: agricultural data that has been combined with other data from various sources and summarized so that the resulting data cannot reasonably be linked to an identified or identifiable agricultural producer, farm, parcel, device, or equipment (Sec. 3(2))
  • Derived data: data that has been significantly modified, processed, analyzed, or compiled, including agronomic insights, reports, and predictive models (Sec. 3(8))
  • Control: a person has the power to avail substantially all benefits from agricultural data, prevent other persons from availing substantially all benefits, and transfer such power to another person (Sec. 4(1))
  • Conversational artificial intelligence service: an artificial intelligence software application, web interface, or computer program that is accessible to the general public and that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through textual, visual, or aural communications, with listed exclusions (Sec. 13(2))
  • Operator: a person who makes available a conversational artificial intelligence service to the public, excluding mobile application stores or search engines solely because they provide access (Sec. 13(6))
  • Minor: an individual that, based upon the circumstance, the operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty is younger than eighteen years of age (Sec. 13(4))
  • Minor account holder: an account holder who is a minor (Sec. 13(5))
  • Account holder: an individual who has, or opens, an account or profile to use a conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 13(1))
  • Sexually explicit conduct and visual depiction: have the same meanings as in 18 U.S.C. 2256 (Sec. 13(8))

Obligations

  • Written consent for the sale of agricultural data shall be obtained through a clear and conspicuous disclosure that is separate from the primary terms of service or data use agreement (Sec. 5(2)).
  • Beginning on January 1, 2027, every new contract or agreement involving the collection or processing of agricultural data in this state shall contain a specific provision stating that the controller or processor is prohibited from engaging in the sale of such agricultural data without the express written consent of the agricultural producer (Sec. 6(1)).
  • Any controller or processor in custody or possession of agricultural data shall establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of such agricultural data (Sec. 7(1)).
  • Such security practices shall be appropriate for the volume and nature of the agricultural data and protect against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or loss (Sec. 7(2)).
  • An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to each minor account holder that such minor account holder is interacting with artificial intelligence as a persistent visible disclaimer or both at the beginning of each session and appearing at least every three hours in a continuous conversational artificial intelligence service interaction (Sec. 14(1)).
  • An operator shall, for minor account holders, institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational artificial intelligence service from producing visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct, generating direct statements that the account holder should engage in sexually explicit conduct, or generating statements that sexually objectify the account holder (Sec. 14(3)).
  • For minor account holders, the operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational artificial intelligence service from generating statements that would lead a reasonable person to believe that they are interacting with a human, including explicit claims that the service is sentient or human, statements that simulate emotional dependence, statements that simulate romantic or sexual innuendos, or role playing of romantic relationships between an adult and a minor (Sec. 14(4)).
  • An operator shall offer tools for minor account holders, and, when such account holders are younger than thirteen years of age, their parents or guardians, to manage the account holders' privacy and account settings; an operator shall also offer related tools to the parents or guardians of minor account holders thirteen years of age and older, as appropriate based on relevant risks (Sec. 14(5)).
  • If a reasonable person interacting with a conversational artificial intelligence service would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, an operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose that the conversational artificial intelligence service is artificial intelligence (Sec. 15).
  • An operator shall adopt a protocol for the conversational artificial intelligence service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self harm that includes, but is not limited to, making reasonable efforts to provide a response to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services (Sec. 16).

Prohibitions

  • A controller or processor shall not engage in the sale of agricultural data without the express written consent of the agricultural producer (Sec. 5(1)).
  • The nonexclusive right of control granted to a controller or processor under section 4 does not include the power to engage in the sale of such agricultural data (Sec. 4(4)).
  • Any contract provision that waives or limits the requirements of the Agricultural Data Privacy Act is contrary to public policy and is void and unenforceable (Sec. 6(2)).
  • An operator shall not provide a minor account holder with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 14(2)).
  • An operator shall not knowingly and intentionally cause or program a conversational artificial intelligence service to make any representation or statement that explicitly indicates that the conversational artificial intelligence service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (Sec. 17).

Penalties and enforcement

For the Agricultural Data Privacy Act, the Attorney General may bring an action in the district court of Lancaster County against any controller or processor that violates the act to seek injunctive relief or recover a civil penalty of one thousand dollars for each separate violation, remitted to the State Treasurer (Sec. 8(1)). The act does not create any new private cause of action, and the Attorney General's enforcement authority is the exclusive remedy (Sec. 8(2)). Before bringing an action to recover a civil penalty for a violation of section 6 or 7, the Attorney General must provide written notice identifying the specific provision; no action may be initiated if within forty five days the controller or processor cures each alleged violation and provides a written statement of cure and future compliance (Sec. 9(1) and (2)). This notice and cure provision does not apply to violations of section 5 (Sec. 9(3)). For the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act, the Attorney General may enforce the act (Sec. 18(1)) and may bring a civil action for appropriate relief on behalf of the State of Nebraska or any person aggrieved by a violation (Sec. 18(2)(a)). Appropriate relief includes preliminary and other equitable or declaratory relief, actual damages, civil penalties of at least one thousand dollars per violation but no more than five hundred thousand dollars per operator, and reasonable expenses including court costs, attorney's fees, investigative costs, witness fees, and deposition costs (Sec. 18(2)(b)). The act does not create a private right of action (Sec. 18(3)), and it does not create liability for the developer of an artificial intelligence model for any violation by a conversational artificial intelligence system developed by a third party operator to provide a service for such developer (Sec. 18(4)).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying AI that collects, stores, or uses agricultural data in Nebraska must treat the agricultural producer as the owner and controller of that data, and the organisation only has a nonexclusive right of control solely for providing services, maintaining equipment, or performing authorized data processing, without any power to sell the data (Sec. 4).
  • Such an organisation must obtain express written consent through a separate clear and conspicuous disclosure before any sale of agricultural data, and new contracts from January 1, 2027 must include a specific no sale provision (Sec. 5, Sec. 6).
  • The organisation must implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices appropriate to the volume and nature of the agricultural data (Sec. 7).
  • An organisation deploying a conversational artificial intelligence service accessible to the general public must comply with disclosure, content prevention, privacy tool, and crisis protocol duties, especially for minor account holders, and must not claim to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (Sec. 14, Sec. 15, Sec. 16, Sec. 17).
  • Violations can lead to Attorney General enforcement, civil penalties, actual damages, and equitable relief, with no private right of action (Sec. 8, Sec. 18).

Notable exemptions

  • Agricultural data does not include aggregated data, derived data, or data made available to the general public by an agency as defined in section 84-901 (Sec. 3(3)(b)).
  • Sale of agricultural data does not include disclosure or transfer to a processor by a controller, use by a processor authorized by a controller, disclosure for providing a service to an agricultural producer, disclosure to an affiliate, disclosure expressly directed in writing by the producer to a designated third party, disclosure required by state or federal law, regulation, subpoena, investigative demand, or court order, disclosure required for compliance with safety, emissions, or environmental obligations, disclosure of information the producer intentionally made available to the general public through mass media without restriction, disclosure as part of a merger, acquisition, bankruptcy, or transaction, or disclosure reasonably necessary to detect, prevent, or respond to fraud, abuse, cybersecurity threat, illegal conduct, data integrity issue, or equipment misuse (Sec. 3(13)(b)).
  • The Agricultural Data Privacy Act shall not be construed to limit or supersede any duty or obligation imposed by federal law or other Nebraska law, relieve any person from any duty or obligation otherwise imposed by law, impair or affect the terms of any private contract in existence prior to the operative date of section 10, or limit or supersede any duty or obligation imposed by a natural resources district operating pursuant to Chapter 2, article 32, any agency as defined in section 84-901, or any employee or agent of such district or agency when acting in performance of a statutory duty (Sec. 10).
  • Conversational artificial intelligence service does not include applications primarily designed and marketed for use by developers or researchers, a feature within another software application that is not a conversational artificial intelligence service, applications designed to provide outputs relating to a narrow and discrete topic, applications primarily designed and marketed for commercial use by business entities, speaker and voice command interfaces or voice activated virtual assistants for consumer electronic devices, applications used by a business solely for internal purposes, or applications used by a business solely for customer service or strictly to provide users with information about available commercial services or products, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to the business's customer service (Sec. 13(2)(b)).
  • Operator does not include mobile application stores or search engines solely because they provide access to a conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 13(6)(b)).
  • The Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act does not create liability for the developer of an artificial intelligence model for any violation by a conversational artificial intelligence system developed by a third party operator to provide a service for such developer (Sec. 18(4)).
  • Agricultural data may be withheld from public records unless prior written consent has been obtained from the owner of such agricultural data under the Agricultural Data Privacy Act (Sec. 11(30)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organisation is a controller or processor of agricultural data collected, produced, or generated in Nebraska, or an operator of a conversational artificial intelligence service accessible to the general public (Sec. 3, Sec. 13).
  • For agricultural data, identify the agricultural producer who owns and controls the data and ensure any collection, storage, or use is limited to providing services, maintaining equipment, or authorized data processing (Sec. 4).
  • Before any sale of agricultural data, obtain express written consent through a clear and conspicuous disclosure separate from the primary terms of service or data use agreement (Sec. 5).
  • For new contracts or agreements involving collection or processing of agricultural data beginning January 1, 2027, include a specific provision stating that the controller or processor is prohibited from selling agricultural data without express written consent (Sec. 6).
  • Establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices appropriate to the volume and nature of the agricultural data (Sec. 7).
  • For conversational artificial intelligence services, implement clear and conspicuous disclosure to minor account holders that they are interacting with artificial intelligence, either as a persistent visible disclaimer or at the beginning of each session and at least every three hours (Sec. 14(1)).
  • Institute reasonable measures to prevent the service from producing sexually explicit visual depictions, direct statements to engage in sexually explicit conduct, or statements that sexually objectify minor account holders, and to prevent statements that would lead a reasonable person to believe they are interacting with a human, including explicit sentience claims, simulated emotional dependence, romantic or sexual innuendos, or romantic role playing between an adult and a minor (Sec. 14(3) and (4)).
  • Offer privacy and account setting tools to minor account holders and their parents or guardians as required (Sec. 14(5)).
  • Adopt a protocol for responding to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self harm that refers users to crisis service providers (Sec. 16).
  • Ensure the service does not knowingly and intentionally represent that it is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (Sec. 17).
  • Prepare for Attorney General enforcement, including responding to any notice and cure opportunity for Agricultural Data Privacy Act sections 6 and 7 within forty five days (Sec. 8, Sec. 9, Sec. 18).
